_comment: 3D mesh library (W5.0b). Composes engine MESH PRIMITIVES (box, sphere, cylinder, capsule, plane, prism, torus, quad — Godot's PrimitiveMesh classes). Each entry is a list of primitives with positions + sizes + $param substitution. Same authoring shape as shapes.json.

house_1f._comment: Kit-of-parts 1-floor cottage (2026-05-27): box body + gable roof + door + 1 window row (front + sides) + chimney. UNIT space (y 0..1); state.scale=[W,H,D]. Paired with the small_house bucket (height ~3.5m) so a fitted ~2m footprint reads as a cottage, NOT a thin tower. $albedo set per instance; roof/door/window/chimney keep defaults.

house_2f._comment: Kit-of-parts 2-floor house: body + gable roof + door + 2 window ROWS + mid trim band (floor divider) + chimney. The two window rows + the divider band make it READ as two storeys at any fitted footprint. Paired with the medium_house bucket (height ~6.5m).

house_3f._comment: Kit-of-parts 3-floor townhouse: body + gable roof + door + 3 window ROWS + 2 trim bands + chimney. Paired with the large_house bucket (height ~9.5m) — the tallest tier still reads as a 3-storey building, not a featureless tower, because of the three window rows + two floor dividers.

tower_kit._comment: Kit-of-parts tower: cylinder shaft + prism (peaked) roof. UNIT space; state.scale=[D,H,D]. $albedo = stone shaft.

fountain_kit._comment: Kit-of-parts fountain: stone basin + central column + water jet. UNIT space. $albedo = stone.

townhall_kit._comment: Kit-of-parts civic hall (2026-05-27): wide base + set-back upper storey + gable roof + 4 front columns + grand door + upper window row + roof finial. UNIT space; state.scale=[W,H,D]. Grander silhouette than houses (two-tier + columns + finial) so it reads as the town's focal building.

bridge_kit._comment: Kit-of-parts bridge: flat deck + two side railings running the span + two end abutments. UNIT space; state.scale=[W,H,D] where D is the span across the river (the longest axis from PCA). $albedo = timber deck.

wall_kit._comment: Kit-of-parts curtain wall: stone body + slightly-overhanging cap + 5 crenellation merlons along the top. UNIT space; state.scale=[length,H,thickness] (length fitted per segment). Merlons run along unit-X so they stretch with the fitted length (wider merlons on longer walls — acceptable). $albedo = stone.

fire_pit_3d._comment: Substantial fire pit — 1.5m diameter stone base + visible log fuel + flame mass. Reads as a 3D structure at distance instead of an icon. Use this for any game needing a proper fire structure; legacy 'fire' mesh (2 small spheres) kept for backward compat.

conifer_tree_3d._comment: Proper conifer — brown trunk + green stacked-sphere canopy. 3m total height. Replaces the merchant_pillar_3d fallback (stone-color pillar) which didn't read as vegetation.

oak_tree_3d._comment: Round broadleaf — bigger trunk, blob canopy. ~3.5m. Distinct silhouette from conifer (round vs triangular).

birch_tree_3d._comment: Slim white-bark tree, sparse pale canopy. ~3m. Light accent against dark conifer mass.

fruit_tree_3d._comment: Apple/berry-bearing broadleaf. Reddish-orange fruit dots on green canopy. Player can identify edible trees at a glance. ~2.8m.

dead_tree_3d._comment: Bare branches, no canopy. Reads as 'old' or 'winter' tree. ~3m. Lighter visual weight — fills space without overwhelming the forest.

water_plane_3d._comment: Flat blue water — 10m × 10m square. Suited for ponds / small lakes. For long flowing rivers use `river_3d` instead. Surface at y=0.05 (no z-fight with ground at y=0).

river_3d._comment: Long flowing river — 6m wide × 50m long (Z axis). Aspect 1:8 reads as 'river' not 'pond.' Three depth bands: sandy bank strips on each side, shallow lighter-blue edges, deeper blue main flow, and a thin centerline ripple highlight. Banks at y=0.02; shallow at y=0.04; main at y=0.06; ripple at y=0.10. Author at any position via instance; use state.yaw to angle the flow, state.scale to stretch (e.g. scale [1, 1, 2] = 100m river).

wolf_3d._comment: Lean grey quadruped — body, 4 legs, head, pointed ears, slim tail. Faces +X. ~1.0m at shoulder × 1.3m long. Wolf-grey palette: charcoal coat, lighter underbelly.

lean_to_3d._comment: Simple shelter — 3 angled logs leaning against an upright + branch-mat roof. ~1.5m × 1.5m × 1.2m. Tilt is implied by stacking boxes diagonally.

fish_trap_3d._comment: Small woven willow basket — cylinder with open top, set on the river bank. ~0.5m diameter × 0.45m tall.

bird_3d._comment: Small bird — central body + 2 wing boxes that flap. ~0.3m wingspan. Wings rotate around their Z axis to read as flapping. Body alone is a tiny sphere so the wings dominate the silhouette. cast_shadow:false — tiny entity at high altitude, shadow invisible.

cloud_3d._comment: Puffy cloud — 4 overlapping white spheres. ~5m wide, drifts slowly via velocity. Per-instance scale via state.scale lets some clouds be bigger (3x) for variety. cast_shadow:false — clouds at y=30 wouldn't render meaningful ground shadows anyway and the cost is wasted.

villager_3d._comment: Humanoid with addressable limbs (ADR 0035). torso/head/4 limbs named so animation_director can swing them. Arm/leg pieces use `pivot` to put the rotation joint at the SHOULDER/HIP (top of limb) instead of the limb's geometric center — otherwise rotating an arm makes the hand AND the shoulder swing in opposite directions through the body. Walk = arm + leg swing in opposing pairs (left arm + right leg forward, then swap). Activates on velocity > 0.5.

animations._comment_idle_silent: Idle actively HOLDS the rest pose so limbs reset when a walking villager stops. Empty tracks would leave limbs frozen mid-stride (animation_director doesn't auto-reset on state switch). Each track is a 1-keyframe 'hold at 0' that overwrites whatever the walk state left behind. Stationary villagers appear perfectly still.

walk._comment_duration: 0.85s/cycle (was 0.55s, felt frantic). 0.85 reads as 'steady walk'; under ~0.7 limbs look hurried; over ~1.1 reads as 'sluggish'.
walk._comment_no_torso_bob: Removed torso translation_y bob (2026-05-15) — user feedback 'body no need shakey when move'. Walk feels grounded without bob; bob reads as 'jittery' rather than 'animated' at low fps.

animation_state_rules._comment_threshold: 0.5 chosen 2026-05-11 after observing wander + schedule attractors emit ~0.25 m/s near-target velocities that kept walk firing perpetually. 0.5 = brisk-walk minimum; idle below.

rabbit_3d._comment: Tiny quadruped — 0.35m tall × 0.4m long. Round white-tail back, small head, two pointy ears. Reads as rabbit at a glance vs other ground props.

berry_bush_3d._comment: Dome shrub with red berries. Green canopy + 5 red berry dots. ~0.7m tall × 1m wide. Reads as 'food shrub' from a distance.

mushroom_patch_3d._comment: Cluster of 4 small brown mushrooms — stem cylinders + dome cap spheres. ~0.4m tall × 0.5m spread. Subdued earth-tone so the BRIGHT red_mushroom variant stands out by contrast.

red_mushroom_3d._comment: SINGLE distinctive red-cap mushroom — bigger than patch siblings so the player notices it. Pale stem + bright red cap with white dots. ~0.5m tall × 0.4m wide. Used by food_red_mushroom (Three Days to Eat hidden rule).

log_pile_3d._comment: Stacked split logs — 3-row pyramid. Bottom row 4 logs, middle row 3, top row 2. ~1.6m wide × 0.9m tall × 0.45m deep. Boxes rather than cylinders because the mesh primitive only does Y-axis cylinders (logs are horizontal). Light/dark wood color alternation gives stack texture.

grass_tuft_3d._comment: Tiny grass tuft — 3 angled blades on a small base. 0.3m wide × 0.4m tall. Scatter densely across village floor for ground texture; reads as 'this isn't bare earth.' cast_shadow:false — at this size shadow contribution is invisible, but each tuft shadow costs as much as its color pass.

deer_3d._comment: Quadruped buck — 4 legs, elongated body, neck, head, simple antlers. ~1.6m tall at antler tips, ~1.0m at back, ~1.5m long. Faces +X by default (head pokes out +X). Warm-brown coat. Reads unambiguously as a 4-legged animal — not human.

market_stall_3d._comment: Market stall — wooden counter + 4 awning poles + striped roof plane. ~2.5m wide × 2.2m tall. Vendor NPC stands behind the counter to read as 'this is the market.'

wall_panel_ns_28._comment: Chamber 1 (Outer Containment) NS wall — 28m wide vs 44m full-chamber wall.

wall_panel_ew_28._comment: Chamber 1 EW wall — 28m deep, oriented along Z axis.

merchant_city_wall_segment_3d._comment: Stone wall segment, 10m long × 4m tall × 1m thick. Tile multiple along perimeter for a continuous wall. Crenellated top (small box pattern) gives medieval keep silhouette.

merchant_city_gate_3d._comment: Wider gate: 2 stone pillars + arched lintel. Place where roads meet city perimeter (4 cardinal gates).

merchant_lamppost_lit_3d._comment: FAT lamppost — 0.3m radius lamp head (was 0.05 — invisible). Per visual-density vocabulary axis 4 (micro-lights every 8-15m, FAT, warm). Two-tone: dark post, bright warm sphere on top.

merchant_npc_hero_3d._comment: Hero / player silhouette — capsule body + cape behind + helm. Distinct from generic townie at glance. Per visual-density axis 10 (silhouette readability).

merchant_npc_shopkeeper_3d._comment: Shopkeeper silhouette — capsule + apron front. Used for supplier stalls + Tomas/Mireille shop owner.

merchant_npc_child_3d._comment: Child silhouette — smaller scale, no hat. For ambient cottage village kids.

merchant_cobblestone_tile_3d._comment: Flat road tile, ~5m square × 5cm thick. Dark-grey cobblestone color. Place in lines for cardinal roads connecting plaza to districts. Use small Y offset so tiles sit on top of the dirt ground without z-fighting.

merchant_plaza_tile_3d._comment: Plaza paving stone, slightly lighter than road tile. Use in 3x3 grid around fountain.

merchant_cottage_small_3d._comment: Small townie cottage variant. 3m × 2.5m × 3m with steep red roof.

merchant_cottage_large_3d._comment: Larger cottage variant. 5m × 3.5m × 4m, brown roof, two windows.

prim_unit_box._comment: Unit box (1x1x1) for compose_world.py. state.scale=[w, h, d] sizes per instance. color=$albedo to recolor.

prim_unit_cylinder._comment: Unit cylinder (radius=0.5, height=1) for compose_world.py. Scale + recolor via state.scale + visual.params.

prim_unit_sphere._comment: Unit sphere (radius=0.5) for compose_world.py. Scale + recolor via state.scale + visual.params.
